bug_semantics: In examples/acf-can/linux/acf-can-listener.c, num_can_msgs is a uint8_t assigned from int avtp_to_can(), which returns -1 on rejection (wrong subtype, stream-id mismatch, invalid ACF, failed Avtp_Can_IsValid, or EFF/CAN-ID inconsistency). The conversion truncates -1 to 255. The subsequent write loop then iterates 255 times over the 15-slot stack array frame_t can_frames[MAX_CAN_FRAMES_IN_ACF] and write()s each slot to the CAN socket, leaking ~18 KB of adjacent stack as ~240 CAN frames. An unauthenticated UDP datagram with the default stream id 0xAABBCCDDEEFF0001 that later fails parsing is sufficient; no authentication exists on this path.
flaw_origin: The truncation-plus-write-loop mechanism was first written in 67fd16fc27be8b5ae852229df743fff8558f4915 (PR #62 member, 2024-12-24 author / 2025-01-05 commit). That commit changed avtp_to_can from a void I/O helper into an int parser that returns a frame count or -1, and it added the Linux listener's uint8_t num_can_msgs, the un-checked assignment, and the for (i < num_can_msgs) CAN write loop. The parent 4412b5d9c371236cb66cb367da0c8c30faf15b27 still called void avtp_to_can(fd, can_socket, ...) with no count variable and no write loop; git grep finds no num_can_msgs in that parent tree. 5d7cf900859548d054125fc5f33a12768a170c31 later dropped the pdu_length argument only. 5ef430d81157e7677fc4e6c62059ad6f7104e9ba converted the sibling linux bridge to int8_t and skipped <=0 returns, but left the listener unchanged until the 2026-08-22 fix.

reasoning: CVE-2026-73523 is a published VulnCheck CVE (CISA ADP enriched, not rejected or withdrawn); GHSA-ggx8-w5hw-4h29 is the GitHub mirror of that record. The sink is integer truncation of avtp_to_can()'s -1 into uint8_t num_can_msgs in the Linux ACF-CAN listener, after which the CAN write loop treats 255 as a valid count and emits stack memory onto the bus. Before 67fd16fc, avtp_to_can was a void function that performed recv/write internally; new_packet()-era -1 returns only aborted processing and never became a write-loop bound. 67fd16fc is therefore the smallest first-write of the complete mechanism (signed-to-unsigned assignment plus unguarded write loop plus -1 returns), even though the subject says 'Refactored': the parent tree contains none of those lines, and GitHub PR #62 preserves 67fd16fc as its own member rather than a squash. Later padding (5d7cf90) and IsValid (e85394e) commits add extra -1 triggers but do not introduce the truncation. The same unsigned pattern in the linux bridge was independently patched in 5ef430d8; that does not change the listener BIC. The fix that closes this CVE is 6744371 on main (PR #161): signed int8_t, skip on <0, extra MAX_CAN_FRAMES_IN_ACF loop cap. It is present on HEAD and in no release tag yet (v0.9.3 still vulnerable). AI attribution is judged only on the BIC commit object, which is human Naresh Nayak with a Signed-off-by trailer and no AI marker; Copilot on the fix PR is irrelevant.
